correctness.rationale: Exact open-neighbor identity, binomial low-degree asymptotics, joint factorial moments, negligible occupied-crossing corrections, and two-sided domination implications prove the paired limits; monotone binomial permutation coupling proves the fixed-size and hitting-time statements. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Dualizing rook cells to bipartite incidence edges preserves the property but does not reduce it to mere minimum degree: odd success needs only one side free of degree-(r-1) vertices, while even success needs both. The familiar Poisson minimum-degree limit alone does not assert this pair of properties; the degree-sum correction and independent deficiency counts must be proved.

value.rationale: A natural reliability gap in randomly placed rook sensors: consecutive odd/even total k requirements share one sharp window but have distinct limiting success laws, a joint mixed outcome law with maximum separation 1/2, and equivalent random-order hitting-time limits. This is a structurally motivated infinite-family probabilistic theorem beyond the known minimum-cardinality problem; exact low-degree obstructions explain the difference.
